File: lstrarch.md
  1 | # LSTR — Detaylı Modül Analizi
  2 | 
  3 | > **Lane Shape Prediction with Transformers** (WACV 2021)  
  4 | > Toplam parametre: **765,787** | MACs: **577M** | CULane F-measure: **~0.64**
  5 | 
  6 | ---
  7 | 
  8 | ## Genel Mimari
  9 | 
 10 | ```mermaid
 11 | flowchart TD
 12 |     IMG["Görüntü\n(B × 3 × H × W)"] --> BACKBONE
 13 |     BACKBONE["🔷 Backbone\nMini-ResNet (4 stage)"] --> FEAT["Feature Map\nB × 128 × h/32 × w/32"]
 14 |     FEAT --> PROJ["input_proj  Conv1×1 → attn_dim"]
 15 |     PROJ --> PE["Position Encoding\n(Sinusoidal)"]
 16 |     PE --> ENC["🔶 Transformer Encoder\n(enc_layers katman)"]
 17 |     ENC --> MEM["Memory (encoded features)"]
 18 |     MEM --> DEC["🔷 Transformer Decoder\n(dec_layers katman)\nnum_queries sorgu emb."]
 19 |     DEC --> HS["Hidden States\nher sorgu için"]
 20 |     HS --> CLS["class_embed  Linear → (num_cls+1)"]
 21 |     HS --> SPEC["specific_embed  MLP → 4 parametre"]
 22 |     HS --> SHR["shared_embed  MLP → 4 paylaşımlı param."]
 23 |     CLS --> OUT["Çıktı: pred_logits + pred_curves"]
 24 |     SPEC --> OUT
 25 |     SHR --> OUT
 26 | ```
 27 | 
 28 | ---
 29 | 
 30 | ## Katman Katman Modül Analizi
 31 | 
 32 | ### 1. Giriş Noktaları
 33 | 
 34 | | Dosya | Görev |
 35 | |-------|-------|
 36 | | `train.py` | Eğitim döngüsü, LR schedule, snapshot kaydetme |
 37 | | `test.py` | Evaluation ve görselleştirme pipeline'ı |
 38 | | `config.py` | Global singleton `system_configs` nesnesi |
 39 | 
 40 | ---
 41 | 
 42 | ### 2. Config Sistemi — `config.py`
 43 | 
 44 | `Config` sınıfı tüm hiperparametreleri merkezi bir sözlükte tutar. JSON config dosyaları `update_config()` ile bu değerleri override eder.
 45 | 
 46 | **CULane için kritik değerler** (`config/LSTR_CULANE.json`):
 47 | 
 48 | | Parametre | Değer | Anlamı |
 49 | |-----------|-------|--------|
 50 | | `res_dims` | [16, 32, 64, 128] | Backbone kanal boyutları |
 51 | | `res_layers` | [1, 2, 2, 2] | Her stage'deki BasicBlock sayısı |
 52 | | `attn_dim` | 32 | Transformer hidden dim |
 53 | | `num_heads` | 2 | Multi-head attention başlık sayısı |
 54 | | `enc_layers` | 2 | Encoder katman sayısı |
 55 | | `dec_layers` | 2 | Decoder katman sayısı |
 56 | | `num_queries` | 7 | Tahmin edilecek şerit adayı sayısı |
 57 | | `dim_feedforward` | 128 | FFN ara katman boyutu |
 58 | | `lsp_dim` | 8 | Şerit parametresi boyutu |
 59 | 
 60 | ---
 61 | 
 62 | ### 3. Model Giriş Noktası — `models/LSTR_CULANE.py`
 63 | 
 64 | `model` ve `loss` sınıflarını tanımlar. `NetworkFactory` bu dosyayı dinamik olarak import eder (`importlib`).
 65 | 
 66 | ```python
 67 | class model(kp):    # kp'den türer, config okuyup super().__init__() çağırır
 68 | class loss(AELoss): # SetCriterion ile Hungarian matching loss
 69 | ```
 70 | 
 71 | ---
 72 | 
 73 | ### 4. Backbone — `models/py_utils/kp.py` → `kp` sınıfı
 74 | 
 75 | **Mini ResNet** — Orijinal ResNet18'den çok küçük, özel kanallarla:
 76 | 
 77 | ```
 78 | Girdi (B, 3, 360, 640)
 79 | │
 80 | ├─ Conv7×7, stride=2      → (B, 16, 180, 320)
 81 | ├─ BN + ReLU + MaxPool    → (B, 16,  90, 160)
 82 | │
 83 | ├─ layer1: 1× BasicBlock(16→16,  stride=1)  → (B,  16, 90, 160)
 84 | ├─ layer2: 2× BasicBlock(16→32,  stride=2)  → (B,  32, 45,  80)
 85 | ├─ layer3: 2× BasicBlock(32→64,  stride=2)  → (B,  64, 23,  40)
 86 | └─ layer4: 2× BasicBlock(64→128, stride=2)  → (B, 128, 12,  20)
 87 | ```
 88 | 
 89 | > `FrozenBatchNorm2d` kullanılır (eğitim sırasında BN istatistikleri freeze).
 90 | 
 91 | **input_proj:** `Conv1×1(128 → attn_dim=32)` — transformer boyutuna düşürür.
 92 | 
 93 | ---
 94 | 
 95 | ### 5. Position Encoding — `models/py_utils/position_encoding.py`
 96 | 
 97 | **Sinusoidal 2D pozisyon kodlaması** (DETR'dan alınmış):
 98 | - Feature map'in her pozisyonuna `(x, y)` için sinüs/kosinüs tabanlı embedding eklenir
 99 | - Transformer'ın konumsal bilgi öğrenmesini sağlar
100 | 
101 | ---
102 | 
103 | ### 6. Transformer — `models/py_utils/transformer.py`
104 | 
105 | DETR'dan uyarlanmış encoder-decoder mimarisi:
106 | 
107 | #### Encoder
108 | ```
109 | Her katmanda:
110 |   ┌─ Self-Attention (q=k=src+pos_embed, v=src)
111 |   ├─ Add & Norm
112 |   ├─ FFN (Linear → ReLU → Linear)
113 |   └─ Add & Norm
114 | ```
115 | - Çıktı: `memory` `(HW × B × C)`
116 | - Dikkat ağırlıkları döndürülür (görselleştirme için)
117 | 
118 | #### Decoder
119 | ```
120 | Her katmanda:
121 |   ┌─ Self-Attention (şerit sorguları arası)
122 |   ├─ Add & Norm
123 |   ├─ Cross-Attention (query=sorgu+query_pos, key=memory+pos)
124 |   ├─ Add & Norm
125 |   ├─ FFN
126 |   └─ Add & Norm
127 | ```
128 | - `num_queries=7` adet sıfır vektörü sorgu olarak başlar
129 | - `return_intermediate=True` ise her decoder katmanından çıktı döner (aux_loss için)
130 | 
131 | ---
132 | 
133 | ### 7. Prediction Heads — `kp.py`
134 | 
135 | Her şerit sorgusu için **3 paralel çıkış kafası**:
136 | 
137 | ```python
138 | class_embed    = Linear(attn_dim, num_cls + 1)          # Sınıf skoru (şerit var/yok)
139 | specific_embed = MLP(attn_dim, attn_dim, 4, mlp_layers)  # Şerite özgü 4 parametre
140 | shared_embed   = MLP(attn_dim, attn_dim, 4, mlp_layers)  # Tüm şeritler için ortak 4 parametre
141 | ```
142 | 
143 | **Şerit Parametresi Formatı** (`pred_curves`, 8 boyutlu):
144 | 
145 | ```
146 | [lower, upper, k'', f'', m'', n', b'', b''']
147 |    0      1     2    3    4    5   6    7
148 | ```
149 | 
150 | Şerit x koordinatı polinomla hesaplanır:
151 | ```
152 | x(y) = k''/(y - f'')² + m''/(y - f'') + n' + b''·y - b'''
153 | ```
154 | 
155 | ---
156 | 
157 | ### 8. Loss Sistemi — `models/py_utils/`
158 | 
159 | #### `matcher.py` — HungarianMatcher
160 | Tahminleri ground-truth şeritlerle **1-to-1 optimal eşleştirme** yapar (scipy `linear_sum_assignment`):
161 | 
162 | ```
163 | Cost = λ_cls · C_class + λ_curves · C_poly + λ_lower · C_lower + λ_upper · C_upper
164 | ```
165 | 
166 | | Ağırlık | Değer | Açıklama |
167 | |---------|-------|----------|
168 | | `loss_ce` | 3 | Sınıflandırma maliyeti |
169 | | `loss_curves` | 5 | Polinom eğri maliyeti |
170 | | `loss_lowers` | 2 | Alt sınır maliyeti |
171 | | `loss_uppers` | 2 | Üst sınır maliyeti |
172 | 
173 | #### `detr_loss.py` — SetCriterion
174 | Eşleştirme sonrasında kayıpları hesaplar:
175 | - **`loss_labels`**: Cross-Entropy (eşleşmeyen sorgular → "no-object" sınıfı)
176 | - **`loss_curves`**: Eşlenen sorgular için L1 polinom kaybı
177 | - **`loss_cardinality`**: Tahmin edilen şerit sayısı kaybı (geri yayılmaz)
178 | 
179 | `aux_loss=True` ile ara decoder katmanlarından da kayıp hesaplanır.
180 | 
181 | ---
182 | 
183 | ### 9. Dataset Pipeline — `db/`
184 | 
185 | ```
186 | db/
187 | ├── detection.py     # Temel DETECTION sınıfı (soyut)
188 | ├── culane.py        # CULANE → CULane veri yükleyici
189 | ├── tusimple.py      # TUSIMPLE → TuSimple veri yükleyici
190 | ├── datasets.py      # {dataset_name: Class} sözlüğü
191 | └── utils/
192 |     ├── lane.py      # LaneEval: TuSimple metrik hesaplama
193 |     └── metric.py    # eval_json yardımcı fonksiyonu
194 | ```
195 | 
196 | **CULANE veri akışı:**
197 | ```
198 | list/*.txt → image path listesi
199 | → _extract_data() → ham şerit koordinatları
200 | → _transform_annotations() → normalize polinom formatına
201 | → pickle cache (./cache/culane_*.pkl)
202 | → DataLoader → model
203 | ```
204 | 
205 | ---
206 | 
207 | ### 10. Training Infrastructure — `nnet/py_factory.py`
208 | 
209 | `NetworkFactory` sınıfı her şeyi sarar:
210 | 
211 | ```
212 | NetworkFactory
213 | ├── model    = DummyModule(LSTR_CULANE.model())
214 | ├── loss     = LSTR_CULANE.loss()
215 | ├── network  = Network(model, loss)   # forward = model + loss
216 | ├── network  = DataParallel(network)  # çoklu GPU desteği
217 | └── optimizer = Adam / SGD / AdamW
218 | ```
219 | 
220 | | Metod | Görev |
221 | |-------|-------|
222 | | `train()` | forward + backward + optimizer.step() |
223 | | `validate()` | `torch.no_grad()` ile kayıp hesaplama |
224 | | `test()` | Sadece model.forward() — kayıp yok |
225 | | `load_params(iter)` | `cache/nnet/LSTR_CULANE/LSTR_CULANE_{iter}.pkl` yükle |
226 | | `save_params(iter)` | Model ağırlıklarını kaydet |
227 | 
228 | ---
229 | 
230 | ### 11. Evaluation Pipeline — `lane_evaluation/`
231 | 
232 | CULane'in resmi C++ evaluator'ı:
233 | 
234 | ```
235 | test.py → .lines.txt dosyaları (results/LSTR_CULANE/500000/testing/)
236 |        ↓
237 | lane_evaluation/evaluate (C++ binary, OpenCV 4.x)
238 |        ↓
239 | tp/fp/fn sayımı (IoU threshold=0.5, lane width=30px)
240 |        ↓
241 | Precision / Recall / F-measure
242 | ```
243 | 
244 | ---
245 | 
246 | ## Tüm Veri Akışı
247 | 
248 | ```
249 | Görüntü (360×640×3)
250 |   → Backbone (Mini-ResNet, 4 stage) ................ (B, 128, 12, 20)
251 |   → Conv1×1 projeksiyon ............................ (B,  32, 12, 20)
252 |   → Sinusoidal 2D Position Encoding
253 |   → Transformer Encoder (2 katman, 2 head) ......... memory
254 |   → Transformer Decoder (2 katman, 7 sorgu) ........ (B,  7, 32)
255 |   ↓
256 |   ┌── class_embed    → (B, 7,  2)   # şerit var/yok skoru
257 |   ├── specific_embed → (B, 7,  4)   # per-lane polinom params
258 |   └── shared_embed   → (B, 7,  4)   # paylaşımlı params (mean)
259 |   ↓
260 | pred_logits : (B, 7, 2)
261 | pred_curves : (B, 7, 8)   [lower, upper, k'', f'', m'', n', b'', b''']
262 |   ↓
263 | [Eğitim]  Hungarian Matching → SetCriterion loss → backward
264 | [Test]    x(y) = k''/(y-f'')² + ...  → .lines.txt → evaluate binary
265 | ```
266 |

File: README.md
  1 | **LSTR**: Lane Shape Prediction with Transformers
  2 | =======
  3 | 
  4 | ![LSTR](.github/logo.png)
  5 | 
  6 | * 😎End-to-end architecture: Directly output lane shape parameters.
  7 | * ⚡Super lightweight: The number of model parameters is only 765,787.
  8 | * ⚡Super low complexity: The number of MACs (1 MAC = 2 FLOP) is only 574.280M.
  9 | * 😎Training friendly: Lower GPU memory cost. Input (360, 640, 3) with batch_size 16 uses 1245MiB GPU usages.
 10 | 
 11 | PyTorch(1.5.0) training, evaluating and pretrained models for LSTR (Lane Shape Prediction with Transformers).
 12 | We streamline the lane detection to a single-stage framework by proposing a novel lane shape model that achieves 96.18
 13 | TuSimple accuracy.
 14 | 
 15 | For details see [End-to-end Lane Shape Prediction with Transformers](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2011.04233.pdf)
 16 | by Ruijin Liu, Zejian Yuan, Tie Liu, Zhiliang Xiong.
 17 | 
 18 | 
 19 | ## LSTR for CULane
 20 | 
 21 | ***Please read carefully!***
 22 | 
 23 | This branch mainly provides training, evaluating and pretrained models of LSTR for CULane dataset.
 24 |  
 25 | * The implement is a vanilla version, and almost all of the hyper-parameters are not fine-tuned.
 26 | The uploaded model file was trained a few days ago, which achieves 0.64 CULane Fmeasure.
 27 | 
 28 | * Our paper does not focus on the CULane dataset, and my point in providing the code and model file 
 29 | is primarily to give you a template to play with other datasets.
 30 | 
 31 | * I may be interesting in tweaking the code to upload code and models that would get better 
 32 | performance, but that's not my top priority right now, so please do not be pushy and ask questions
 33 | about how to improve the performance on CULane dataset.
 34 | 
 35 | ## Model Zoo
 36 | 
 37 | We provide the baseline LSTR_CULANE model file (trained on CULane train and val sets after 500000 iterations) in
 38 | the ./cache/nnet/LSTR_CULANE/LSTR_CULANE_500000.pkl (~3.1MB).
 39 | 
 40 | ## Data Preparation
 41 | 
 42 | Download and extract CULane train, val and test with annotations from
 43 | [CULane](https://xingangpan.github.io/projects/CULane.html).
 44 | 
 45 | We expect the directory structure to be the following:
 46 | ```
 47 | CULane/
 48 |     driver_23_30frame/
 49 |     driver_37_30frame/
 50 |     driver_100_30frame/
 51 |     driver_161_90frame/
 52 |     driver_182_30frame/
 53 |     driver_193_90frame/
 54 |     list/
 55 |         test_split/
 56 |         test.txt
 57 |         test_img.txt
 58 |         train.txt
 59 |         train_gt.txt
 60 |         val.txt
 61 |         val_gt.txt
 62 | TuSimple/
 63 |     LaneDetection/
 64 |         clips/
 65 |         label_data_0313.json
 66 |         label_data_0531.json
 67 |         label_data_0601.json
 68 |         test_label.json
 69 |     LSTR/
 70 | ```
 71 | 
 72 | ## Set Envirionment
 73 | 
 74 | * Linux ubuntu 16.04
 75 | 
 76 | 
 77 | ```
 78 | conda env create --name lstr --file environment.txt
 79 | ```
 80 | 
 81 | After you create the environment, activate it
 82 | 
 83 | ```
 84 | conda activate lstr
 85 | ```
 86 | 
 87 | Then
 88 | 
 89 | ```
 90 | pip install -r requirements.txt
 91 | ```
 92 | 
 93 | ## Training and Evaluation
 94 | 
 95 | To train a model:
 96 | 
 97 | (if you only want to use the train set, please see ./config/LSTR_CULANE.json and
 98 | set "train_split": "train")
 99 | ```
100 | python train.py LSTR_CULANE
101 | ```
102 | * Visualized images are in ./results during training.
103 | * Saved model files (every 5000 iterations) are in ./cache during training.
104 | 
105 | To train a model from a snapshot model file:
106 | ```
107 | python train.py LSTR_CULANE --iter 500000
108 | ```
109 | 
110 | To evaluate (GPU 603MiB usage when evaluating single image iteratively):
111 | ```
112 | python test.py LSTR_CULANE --testiter 500000 --modality eval --split testing
113 | ```
114 | then 
115 | ```
116 | cd lane_evaluation
117 | ```
118 | If you want to obtain the overall F1-measure:
119 | ```
120 | bash run.sh
121 | ```
122 | If you want to valid the splitting performance:
123 | ```
124 | bash Run.sh
125 | ```
126 | Please refer to [CULane](https://xingangpan.github.io/projects/CULane.html) to compile the evaluating environment.
127 | 
128 | 
129 | To evaluate and save detected images in ./results/LSTR_CULANE/500000/testing/lane_debug:
130 | ```
131 | python test.py LSTR_CULANE --testiter 500000 --modality eval --split testing --debug
132 | ```
133 | 
134 | * Demo (displayed parameters are rounded to three significant figures.)
135 | 
136 | ![Demo](.github/driver_100_30frame_05251609_0446.MP4_03330.jpg)
137 | 
138 | ![Demo](.github/driver_100_30frame_05251627_0452.MP4_04020.jpg)
139 | 
140 | ![Demo](.github/driver_100_30frame_05251642_0457.MP4_04620.jpg)
141 | 
142 | 
143 | To evaluate and save decoder attention maps (store --debugEnc to visualize encoder attention maps):
144 | ```
145 | python test.py LSTR_CULANE --testiter 500000 --modality eval --split testing --debug --debugDec
146 | ```
147 | 
148 | To evaluate on a set of images (store your images in ./images, then the detected results will be saved in ./detections):
149 | ```
150 | python test.py LSTR_CULANE --testiter 500000 --modality images --image_root ./ --debug
151 | ```
152 |

 44 | def prefetch_data(db, queue, sample_data):
 45 |     ind = 0
 46 |     print("start prefetching data...")
 47 |     np.random.seed(os.getpid())
 48 |     while True:
 49 |         try:
 50 |             data, ind = sample_data(db, ind)
 51 |             queue.put(data)
 52 |         except Exception as e:
 53 |             traceback.print_exc()
 54 |             raise e
 55 | 
 56 | def pin_memory(data_queue, pinned_data_queue, sema):
 57 |     while True:
 58 |         data = data_queue.get()
 59 | 
 60 |         data["xs"] = [x.pin_memory() for x in data["xs"]]
 61 |         data["ys"] = [y.pin_memory() for y in data["ys"]]
 62 | 
 63 |         pinned_data_queue.put(data)
 64 | 
 65 |         if sema.acquire(blocking=False):
 66 |             return
 67 | 
 68 | def init_parallel_jobs(dbs, queue, fn):
 69 |     tasks = [Process(target=prefetch_data, args=(db, queue, fn)) for db in dbs]
 70 |     for task in tasks:
 71 |         task.daemon = True
 72 |         task.start()
 73 |     return tasks

 54 | class Bottleneck(nn.Module):
 55 |     # Bottleneck in torchvision places the stride for downsampling at 3x3 convolution(self.conv2)
 56 |     # while original implementation places the stride at the first 1x1 convolution(self.conv1)
 57 |     # according to "Deep residual learning for image recognition"https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.03385.
 58 |     # This variant is also known as ResNet V1.5 and improves accuracy according to
 59 |     # https://ngc.nvidia.com/catalog/model-scripts/nvidia:resnet_50_v1_5_for_pytorch.
 60 | 
 61 |     expansion = 4
 62 | 
 63 |     def __init__(self, inplanes, planes, stride=1, downsample=None, groups=1,
 64 |                  base_width=64, dilation=1, norm_layer=None):
 65 |         super(Bottleneck, self).__init__()
 66 |         if norm_layer is None:
 67 |             norm_layer = nn.BatchNorm2d
 68 |         width = int(planes * (base_width / 64.)) * groups
 69 |         # Both self.conv2 and self.downsample layers downsample the input when stride != 1
 70 |         self.conv1 = conv1x1(inplanes, width)
 71 |         self.bn1 = norm_layer(width)
 72 |         self.conv2 = conv3x3(width, width, stride, groups, dilation)
 73 |         self.bn2 = norm_layer(width)
 74 |         self.conv3 = conv1x1(width, planes * self.expansion)
 75 |         self.bn3 = norm_layer(planes * self.expansion)
 76 |         self.relu = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
 77 |         self.downsample = downsample
 78 |         self.stride = stride
 79 | 
 80 |     def forward(self, x):
 81 |         identity = x
 82 | 
 83 |         out = self.conv1(x)
 84 |         out = self.bn1(out)
 85 |         out = self.relu(out)
 86 | 
 87 |         out = self.conv2(out)
 88 |         out = self.bn2(out)
 89 |         out = self.relu(out)
 90 | 
 91 |         out = self.conv3(out)
 92 |         out = self.bn3(out)
 93 | 
 94 |         if self.downsample is not None:
 95 |             identity = self.downsample(x)
 96 | 
 97 |         out += identity
 98 |         out = self.relu(out)
 99 | 
100 |         return out

 19 | class FrozenBatchNorm2d(torch.nn.Module):
 20 |     """
 21 |     BatchNorm2d where the batch statistics and the affine parameters are fixed.
 22 | 
 23 |     Copy-paste from torchvision.misc.ops with added eps before rqsrt,
 24 |     without which any other models than torchvision.models.resnet[18,34,50,101]
 25 |     produce nans.
 26 |     """
 27 | 
 28 |     def __init__(self, n):
 29 |         super(FrozenBatchNorm2d, self).__init__()
 30 |         self.register_buffer("weight", torch.ones(n))
 31 |         self.register_buffer("bias", torch.zeros(n))
 32 |         self.register_buffer("running_mean", torch.zeros(n))
 33 |         self.register_buffer("running_var", torch.ones(n))
 34 | 
 35 |     def _load_from_state_dict(self, state_dict, prefix, local_metadata, strict,
 36 |                               missing_keys, unexpected_keys, error_msgs):
 37 |         num_batches_tracked_key = prefix + 'num_batches_tracked'
 38 |         if num_batches_tracked_key in state_dict:
 39 |             del state_dict[num_batches_tracked_key]
 40 | 
 41 |         super(FrozenBatchNorm2d, self)._load_from_state_dict(
 42 |             state_dict, prefix, local_metadata, strict,
 43 |             missing_keys, unexpected_keys, error_msgs)
 44 | 
 45 |     def forward(self, x):
 46 |         # move reshapes to the beginning
 47 |         # to make it fuser-friendly
 48 |         w = self.weight.reshape(1, -1, 1, 1)
 49 |         b = self.bias.reshape(1, -1, 1, 1)
 50 |         rv = self.running_var.reshape(1, -1, 1, 1)
 51 |         rm = self.running_mean.reshape(1, -1, 1, 1)
 52 |         eps = 1e-5
 53 |         scale = w * (rv + eps).rsqrt()
 54 |         bias = b - rm * scale
 55 |         return x * scale + bias

 62 | class MLP(nn.Module):
 63 |     """ Very simple multi-layer perceptron (also called FFN)"""
 64 | 
 65 |     def __init__(self, input_dim, hidden_dim, output_dim, num_layers):
 66 |         super().__init__()
 67 |         self.num_layers = num_layers
 68 |         h = [hidden_dim] * (num_layers - 1)
 69 |         self.layers = nn.ModuleList(nn.Linear(n, k) for n, k in zip([input_dim] + h, h + [output_dim]))
 70 | 
 71 |     def forward(self, x):
 72 |         for i, layer in enumerate(self.layers):
 73 |             x = F.relu(layer(x)) if i < self.num_layers - 1 else layer(x)
 74 |         return x

167 |         downsample = None

173 |             )

 18 | class Transformer(nn.Module):
 19 | 
 20 |     def __init__(self, d_model=512, nhead=8, num_encoder_layers=6,
 21 |                  num_decoder_layers=6, dim_feedforward=2048, dropout=0.1,
 22 |                  activation="relu", normalize_before=False,
 23 |                  return_intermediate_dec=False):
 24 |         super().__init__()
 25 |         encoder_layer = TransformerEncoderLayer(d_model, nhead, dim_feedforward,
 26 |                                                 dropout, activation, normalize_before)
 27 |         encoder_norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model) if normalize_before else None
 28 |         self.encoder = TransformerEncoder(encoder_layer, num_encoder_layers, encoder_norm)  # layer, 6, norm
 29 | 
 30 |         decoder_layer = TransformerDecoderLayer(d_model, nhead, dim_feedforward,
 31 |                                                 dropout, activation, normalize_before)
 32 |         decoder_norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
 33 |         self.decoder = TransformerDecoder(decoder_layer, num_decoder_layers, decoder_norm,
 34 |                                           return_intermediate=return_intermediate_dec)

 41 |     def _reset_parameters(self):
 42 |         for p in self.parameters():
 43 |             if p.dim() > 1:
 44 |                 nn.init.xavier_uniform_(p)
 45 | 
 46 |     def forward(self, src, mask, query_embed, pos_embed):
 47 |         # flatten NxCxHxW to HWxNxC
 48 |         bs, c, h, w = src.shape
 49 |         src = src.flatten(2).permute(2, 0, 1)
 50 | 
 51 |         pos_embed = pos_embed.flatten(2).permute(2, 0, 1)
 52 | 
 53 |         query_embed = query_embed.unsqueeze(1).repeat(1, bs, 1)
 54 | 
 55 |         mask = mask.flatten(1)
 56 | 
 57 |         tgt = torch.zeros_like(query_embed)
 58 | 
 59 |         memory, weights = self.encoder(src, src_key_padding_mask=mask, pos=pos_embed)
 60 | 
 61 |         hs = self.decoder(tgt, memory, memory_key_padding_mask=mask,
 62 |                           pos=pos_embed, query_pos=query_embed)
 63 | 
 64 |         return hs.transpose(1, 2), memory.permute(1, 2, 0).view(bs, c, h, w), weights

 67 | class TransformerEncoder(nn.Module):
 68 | 
 69 |     def __init__(self, encoder_layer, num_layers, norm=None):
 70 |         super().__init__()
 71 |         self.layers = _get_clones(encoder_layer, num_layers)
 72 |         self.num_layers = num_layers
 73 |         self.norm = norm
 74 | 
 75 |     def forward(self, src,
 76 |                 mask: Optional[Tensor] = None,
 77 |                 src_key_padding_mask: Optional[Tensor] = None,
 78 |                 pos: Optional[Tensor] = None):
 79 |         output = src
 80 | 
 81 |         for layer in self.layers:
 82 | 
 83 |             output, weights = layer(output, src_mask=mask,
 84 |                            src_key_padding_mask=src_key_padding_mask, pos=pos)
 85 | 
 86 |         if self.norm is not None:
 87 |             output = self.norm(output)
 88 | 
 89 |         return output, weights

 92 | class TransformerDecoder(nn.Module):
 93 | 
 94 |     def __init__(self, decoder_layer, num_layers, norm=None, return_intermediate=False):
 95 |         super().__init__()
 96 |         self.layers = _get_clones(decoder_layer, num_layers)
 97 |         self.num_layers = num_layers
 98 |         self.norm = norm
 99 |         self.return_intermediate = return_intermediate
100 | 
101 |     def forward(self, tgt, memory,
102 |                 tgt_mask: Optional[Tensor] = None,
103 |                 memory_mask: Optional[Tensor] = None,
104 |                 tgt_key_padding_mask: Optional[Tensor] = None,
105 |                 memory_key_padding_mask: Optional[Tensor] = None,
106 |                 pos: Optional[Tensor] = None,
107 |                 query_pos: Optional[Tensor] = None):
108 |         output = tgt
109 | 
110 |         intermediate = []
111 | 
112 |         for layer in self.layers:
113 |             output = layer(output, memory, tgt_mask=tgt_mask,
114 |                            memory_mask=memory_mask,
115 |                            tgt_key_padding_mask=tgt_key_padding_mask,
116 |                            memory_key_padding_mask=memory_key_padding_mask,
117 |                            pos=pos, query_pos=query_pos)
118 |             if self.return_intermediate:
119 |                 intermediate.append(self.norm(output))
120 | 
121 |         if self.norm is not None:
122 |             output = self.norm(output)
123 |             if self.return_intermediate:
124 |                 intermediate.pop()
125 |                 intermediate.append(output)
126 | 
127 |         if self.return_intermediate:
128 |             return torch.stack(intermediate)
129 | 
130 |         return output

149 |         self.activation = _get_activation_fn(activation)

155 |     def forward_post(self,
156 |                      src,
157 |                      src_mask: Optional[Tensor] = None,

160 |         q = k = self.with_pos_embed(src, pos)

 10 | class SetCriterion(nn.Module):
 11 |     """ This class computes the loss for DETR.
 12 |     The process happens in two steps:
 13 |         1) we compute hungarian assignment between ground truth boxes and the outputs of the model
 14 |         2) we supervise each pair of matched ground-truth / prediction (supervise class and box)
 15 |     """
 16 |     def __init__(self, num_classes, matcher, weight_dict, eos_coef, losses):
 17 |         """ Create the criterion.
 18 |         Parameters:
 19 |             num_classes: number of object categories, omitting the special no-object category
 20 |             matcher: module able to compute a matching between targets and proposals
 21 |             weight_dict: dict containing as key the names of the losses and as values their relative weight.
 22 |             eos_coef: relative classification weight applied to the no-object category
 23 |             losses: list of all the losses to be applied. See get_loss for list of available losses.
 24 |         """
 25 |         super().__init__()
 26 |         self.num_classes = num_classes

 38 |     def loss_labels(self, outputs, targets, indices, num_curves, log=True):

 40 |         targets dicts must contain the key "labels" containing a tensor of dim [nb_target_boxes]

 46 |         target_classes = torch.full(src_logits.shape[:2], self.num_classes, dtype=torch.int64, device=src_logits.device)
 47 |         target_classes[idx] = target_classes_o
 48 |         loss_ce = F.cross_entropy(src_logits.transpose(1, 2), target_classes, self.empty_weight)
 49 |         losses = {'loss_ce': loss_ce}

 51 |         if log:
 52 |             # TODO this should probably be a separate loss, not hacked in this one here
 53 |             losses['class_error'] = 100 - accuracy(src_logits[idx], target_classes_o)[0]

 56 |     @torch.no_grad()
 57 |     def loss_cardinality(self, outputs, targets, indices, num_curves):
 58 |         """ Compute the cardinality error, ie the absolute error in the number of predicted non-empty boxes
 59 |         This is not really a loss, it is intended for logging purposes only. It doesn't propagate gradients
 60 |         """
 61 |         pred_logits = outputs['pred_logits']
 62 |         device = pred_logits.device
 63 |         tgt_lengths = torch.as_tensor([tgt.shape[0] for tgt in targets], device=device)
 64 |         card_pred = (pred_logits.argmax(-1) != pred_logits.shape[-1] - 1).sum(1)
 65 |         card_err = F.l1_loss(card_pred.float(), tgt_lengths.float())
 66 |         losses = {'cardinality_error': card_err}
 67 |         return losses

 69 |     def loss_curves(self, outputs, targets, indices, num_curves):
 70 |         """Compute the losses related to the bounding boxes, the L1 regression loss and the GIoU loss
 71 |            targets dicts must contain the key "boxes" containing a tensor of dim [nb_target_boxes, 4]

 75 |         idx = self._get_src_permutation_idx(indices)

131 |     def forward(self, outputs, targets):
132 |         """ This performs the loss computation.
133 |         Parameters:
134 |              outputs: dict of tensors, see the output specification of the model for the format
135 |              targets: list of dicts, such that len(targets) == batch_size.
136 |                       The expected keys in each dict depends on the losses applied, see each loss' doc
137 |         """
138 |         outputs_without_aux = {k: v for k, v in outputs.items() if k != 'aux_outputs'}
139 | 
140 |         # Retrieve the matching between the outputs of the last layer and the targets
141 |         indices = self.matcher(outputs_without_aux, targets)
142 | 
143 |         # Compute the average number of target boxes accross all nodes, for normalization purposes
144 |         num_curves = sum(tgt.shape[0] for tgt in targets)
145 |         num_curves = torch.as_tensor([num_curves], dtype=torch.float, device=next(iter(outputs.values())).device)
146 |         if is_dist_avail_and_initialized():
147 |             torch.distributed.all_reduce(num_curves)
148 |         num_curves = torch.clamp(num_curves / get_world_size(), min=1).item()
149 | 
150 |         # Compute all the requested losses
151 |         losses = {}
152 |         for loss in self.losses:
153 |             losses.update(self.get_loss(loss, outputs, targets, indices, num_curves))
154 | 
155 |         # In case of auxiliary losses, we repeat this process with the output of each intermediate layer.
156 |         if 'aux_outputs' in outputs:
157 |             for i, aux_outputs in enumerate(outputs['aux_outputs']):
158 |                 indices = self.matcher(aux_outputs, targets)
159 |                 for loss in self.losses:
160 |                     if loss == 'masks':
161 |                         # Intermediate masks losses are too costly to compute, we ignore them.
162 |                         continue
163 |                     kwargs = {}
164 |                     if loss == 'labels':
165 |                         # Logging is enabled only for the last layer
166 |                         kwargs = {'log': False}
167 |                     l_dict = self.get_loss(loss, aux_outputs, targets, indices, num_curves, **kwargs)
168 |                     l_dict = {k + f'_{i}': v for k, v in l_dict.items()}
169 |                     losses.update(l_dict)
170 | 
171 |         return losses, indices

10 | class HungarianMatcher(nn.Module):
11 |     """This class computes an assignment between the targets and the predictions of the network
12 | 
13 |     For efficiency reasons, the targets don't include the no_object. Because of this, in general,
14 |     there are more predictions than targets. In this case, we do a 1-to-1 matching of the best predictions,
15 |     while the others are un-matched (and thus treated as non-objects).
16 |     """
17 | 
18 |     def __init__(self, cost_class: float = 1,
19 |                  curves_weight: float = 1, lower_weight: float = 1, upper_weight: float = 1):
20 |         """Creates the matcher
21 |         """
22 | 
23 |         super().__init__()
24 |         self.cost_class = cost_class
25 |         threshold = 15 / 720.
26 |         self.threshold = nn.Threshold(threshold**2, 0.)
27 | 
28 |         self.curves_weight = curves_weight
29 |         self.lower_weight = lower_weight
30 |         self.upper_weight = upper_weight
31 | 
32 |     @torch.no_grad()
33 |     def forward(self, outputs, targets):
34 |         """ Performs the matching
35 |         """
36 |         bs, num_queries = outputs["pred_logits"].shape[:2]
37 | 
38 |         # We flatten to compute the cost matrices in a batch
39 |         out_prob = outputs["pred_logits"].flatten(0, 1).softmax(-1)
40 |         tgt_ids  = torch.cat([tgt[:, 0] for tgt in targets]).long()
41 | 
42 |         # Compute the classification cost. Contrary to the loss, we don't use the NLL,
43 |         # but approximate it in 1 - proba[target class].
44 |         # The 1 is a constant that doesn't change the matching, it can be ommitted.
45 |         cost_class = -out_prob[:, tgt_ids]
46 | 
47 |         out_bbox = outputs["pred_curves"]
48 |         tgt_uppers = torch.cat([tgt[:, 2] for tgt in targets])
49 |         tgt_lowers = torch.cat([tgt[:, 1] for tgt in targets])
50 | 
51 |         # # Compute the L1 cost between lowers and uppers
52 |         cost_lower = torch.cdist(out_bbox[:, :, 0].view((-1, 1)), tgt_lowers.unsqueeze(-1), p=1)
53 |         cost_upper = torch.cdist(out_bbox[:, :, 1].view((-1, 1)), tgt_uppers.unsqueeze(-1), p=1)
54 | 
55 |         # # Compute the poly cost
56 |         tgt_points = torch.cat([tgt[:, 3:] for tgt in targets]) # 0~20 112
57 |         tgt_xs = tgt_points[:, :tgt_points.shape[1] // 2]
58 |         valid_xs = tgt_xs >= 0
59 |         weights = (torch.sum(valid_xs, dtype=torch.float32) / torch.sum(valid_xs, dim=1, dtype=torch.float32))**0.5
60 |         weights = weights / torch.max(weights)
61 | 
62 |         tgt_ys = tgt_points[:, tgt_points.shape[1] // 2:]
63 |         out_polys = out_bbox[:, :, 2:].view((-1, 6))
64 |         tgt_ys = tgt_ys.repeat(out_polys.shape[0], 1, 1)
65 |         tgt_ys = tgt_ys.transpose(0, 2)
66 |         tgt_ys = tgt_ys.transpose(0, 1)
67 | 
68 |         # Calculate the predicted xs
69 |         out_xs = out_polys[:, 0] / (tgt_ys - out_polys[:, 1]) ** 2 + out_polys[:, 2] / (tgt_ys - out_polys[:, 1]) + \
70 |                  out_polys[:, 3] + out_polys[:, 4] * tgt_ys - out_polys[:, 5]
71 |         tgt_xs = tgt_xs.repeat(out_polys.shape[0], 1, 1)
72 |         tgt_xs = tgt_xs.transpose(0, 2)
73 |         tgt_xs = tgt_xs.transpose(0, 1)
74 | 
75 |         cost_polys = torch.stack([torch.sum(torch.abs(tgt_x[valid_x] - out_x[valid_x]), dim=0) for tgt_x, out_x, valid_x in zip(tgt_xs, out_xs, valid_xs)], dim=-1)
76 |         cost_polys = cost_polys * weights
77 | 
78 |         # # Final cost matrix
79 |         C = self.cost_class * cost_class + self.curves_weight * cost_polys + \
80 |             self.lower_weight * cost_lower + self.upper_weight * cost_upper
81 | 
82 |         C = C.view(bs, num_queries, -1).cpu()
83 | 
84 |         sizes = [tgt.shape[0] for tgt in targets]
85 | 
86 |         indices = [linear_sum_assignment(c[i]) for i, c in enumerate(C.split(sizes, -1))]
87 |         return [(torch.as_tensor(i, dtype=torch.int64), torch.as_tensor(j, dtype=torch.int64)) for i, j in indices]
88 |

 15 |     used by the Attention is all you need paper, generalized to work on images.
 16 |     """
 17 |     def __init__(self, num_pos_feats=64, temperature=10000, normalize=False, scale=None):
 18 |         super().__init__()
 19 |         self.num_pos_feats = num_pos_feats  # 128
 20 |         self.temperature = temperature  # 10000
 21 |         self.normalize = normalize   # True
 22 | 
 23 |         if scale is not None and normalize is False:
 24 |             raise ValueError("normalize should be True if scale is passed")
 25 |         if scale is None:
 26 |             scale = 2 * math.pi
 27 |         self.scale = scale  # 2pi
 28 | 
 29 |     def forward(self, x, mask):
 30 |         # x = tensor_list.tensors
 31 |         # mask = tensor_list.mask  # the image location which is padded with 0 is set to be 1 at the corresponding mask location
 32 |         assert mask is not None
 33 |         not_mask = ~mask  # image 0 -> 0
 34 | 
 35 |         y_embed = not_mask.cumsum(1, dtype=torch.float32)
 36 |         x_embed = not_mask.cumsum(2, dtype=torch.float32)
 37 | 
 38 |         if self.normalize:
 39 |             eps = 1e-6
 40 |             y_embed = y_embed / (y_embed[:, -1:, :] + eps) * self.scale
 41 |             x_embed = x_embed / (x_embed[:, :, -1:] + eps) * self.scale
 42 | 
 43 | 
 44 |         dim_t = torch.arange(self.num_pos_feats, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
 45 | 
 46 |         dim_t = self.temperature ** (2 * (dim_t // 2) / self.num_pos_feats)
 47 | 
 48 |         pos_x = x_embed[:, :, :, None] / dim_t
 49 |         pos_y = y_embed[:, :, :, None] / dim_t
 50 | 
 51 |         pos_x = torch.stack((pos_x[:, :, :, 0::2].sin(), pos_x[:, :, :, 1::2].cos()), dim=4).flatten(3)
 52 |         pos_y = torch.stack((pos_y[:, :, :, 0::2].sin(), pos_y[:, :, :, 1::2].cos()), dim=4).flatten(3)
 53 | 
 54 |         pos = torch.cat((pos_y, pos_x), dim=3).permute(0, 3, 1, 2)
 55 | 
 56 |         return pos
 57 | 
 58 | 
 59 | class PositionEmbeddingLearned(nn.Module):
 60 |     """
 61 |     Absolute pos embedding, learned.
 62 |     """
 63 |     def __init__(self, num_pos_feats=256):
 64 |         super().__init__()
 65 |         self.row_embed = nn.Embedding(50, num_pos_feats)
 66 |         self.col_embed = nn.Embedding(50, num_pos_feats)
 67 |         self.reset_parameters()
 68 | 
 69 |     def reset_parameters(self):
 70 |         nn.init.uniform_(self.row_embed.weight)
 71 |         nn.init.uniform_(self.col_embed.weight)
 72 | 
 73 |     def forward(self, tensor_list):
 74 |         x = tensor_list.tensors
 75 |         h, w = x.shape[-2:]
 76 |         i = torch.arange(w, device=x.device)
 77 |         j = torch.arange(h, device=x.device)
 78 |         x_emb = self.col_embed(i)
 79 |         y_emb = self.row_embed(j)
 80 |         pos = torch.cat([
 81 |             x_emb.unsqueeze(0).repeat(h, 1, 1),
 82 |             y_emb.unsqueeze(1).repeat(1, w, 1),
 83 |         ], dim=-1).permute(2, 0, 1).unsqueeze(0).repeat(x.shape[0], 1, 1, 1)
 84 |         return pos
 85 | 
 86 | 
 87 | def build_position_encoding(hidden_dim, type):
 88 |     N_steps = hidden_dim // 2
 89 |     if type in ('v2', 'sine'):
 90 |         # TODO find a better way of exposing other arguments
 91 |         position_embedding = PositionEmbeddingSine(N_steps, normalize=True)
 92 | 
 93 |     elif type in ('v3', 'learned'):
 94 |         position_embedding = PositionEmbeddingLearned(N_steps)
 95 | 
 96 |     else:
 97 |         raise ValueError(f"not supported {type}")
 98 | 
 99 |     return position_embedding

207 |         if img_wh is None:

209 |             img_w = self._get_img_width(anno['path'])

214 |         old_lanes = zip(old_lanes, categories)

216 |         lanes = np.ones((self.max_lanes, 1 + 2 + 2 * self.max_points), dtype=np.float32) * -1e5
217 |         lanes[:, 0] = 0

219 |         for lane_pos, (lane, category) in enumerate(old_lanes):
220 |             lower, upper = lane[0][1], lane[-1][1]

222 |             ys = np.array([p[1] for p in lane]) / img_h

225 |             lanes[lane_pos, 2] = upper / img_h
226 |             lanes[lane_pos, 3:3 + len(xs)] = xs
227 |             lanes[lane_pos, (3 + self.max_points):(3 + self.max_points + len(ys))] = ys
228 | 
229 |         new_anno = {
230 |             'path': anno['path'],
231 |             'label': lanes,
232 |             'old_anno': anno,

263 |         y_samples = []

275 |             lane_pred[ys < lane[2]] = 0
276 | 
277 |             lane_pred[(lane_pred < 0) | (lane_pred > self.img_w - 1)] = 0
278 | 
279 |             if np.sum(lane_pred > 0) < 2:
280 |                 lane_pred = np.zeros_like(lane_pred)

416 |     def pred2culaneformat(self, idx, pred, runtime, exp_dir):
417 |         runtime *= 1000.  # s to ms
418 |         img_name = self._annotations[idx]['old_anno']['org_path']  # /driver_100_30frame/05251517_0433.MP4/00930.jpg
419 |         h_samples = self._annotations[idx]['old_anno']['y_samples']  # no need
420 |         lanes = self.pred2lanes(img_name, pred, h_samples)
421 |         prefix = os.path.dirname(img_name)
422 |         prefix = os.path.join(exp_dir, prefix[1:])
423 |         if not os.path.exists(prefix) and prefix != '':
424 |             os.makedirs(prefix)
425 |         save_name = os.path.join(exp_dir, img_name[1:-4] + '.lines.txt')
426 |         with open(save_name, 'w') as fp:
427 |             for lane in lanes:
428 |                 if np.sum(lane > 0) > 1:
429 |                     for ind, x in enumerate(lane):

 39 | class PostProcess(nn.Module):
 40 |     """ This module converts the model's output into the format expected by the coco api"""
 41 |     @torch.no_grad()
 42 |     def forward(self, outputs, target_sizes):
 43 |         """ Perform the computation
 44 |         Parameters:
 45 |             outputs: raw outputs of the model
 46 |             target_sizes: tensor of dimension [batch_size x 2] containing the size of each images of the batch
 47 |                           For evaluation, this must be the original image size (before any data augmentation)
 48 |                           For visualization, this should be the image size after data augment, but before padding
 49 |         """
 50 |         out_logits, out_bbox = outputs['pred_logits'], outputs['pred_curves']
 51 |         assert len(out_logits) == len(target_sizes)
 52 |         assert target_sizes.shape[1] == 2
 53 |         prob = F.softmax(out_logits, -1)
 54 |         scores, labels = prob.max(-1)
 55 |         labels[labels != 1] = 0
 56 |         results = torch.cat([labels.unsqueeze(-1).float(), out_bbox], dim=-1)
 57 | 
 58 |         return results

Result: LSTR projesinin kaynak kodlarını detaylı olarak inceledim. İşte kapsamlı analiz:

## 📋 PROJE YAPISI

### 🎯 Genel Bakış
**LSTR (Lane Shape Prediction with Transformers)** - WACV 2021
- Transformer tabanlı şerit tespiti modeli
- End-to-end mimari: Doğrudan şerit parametrelerini tahmin eder
- Çok hafif: **765,787 parametre**, **574M MACs**
- CULane F-measure: **~0.64**

---

## 🏗️ MİMARİ BİLEŞENLER

### 1. Konfigürasyon Sistemi ([`config.py`](config.py:1))
- [`Config`](config.py:4) sınıfı: Merkezi parametre yönetimi
- JSON dosyalarla override: [`LSTR_CULANE.json`](config/LSTR_CULANE.json:1)
- **Kritik parametreler**:
  - `res_dims`: [16, 32, 64, 128] - Mini-ResNet kanalları
  - `attn_dim`: 32 - Transformer hidden dim
  - `num_queries`: 7 - Şerit aday sayısı
  - `enc_layers/dec_layers`: 2 - Encoder/Decoder katmanları
  - `num_heads`: 2 - Multi-head attention

### 2. Backbone ([`models/py_utils/kp.py`](models/py_utils/kp.py:107))
**Mini-ResNet** (Standart ResNet18'den çok küçük):
```
Girdi: (B, 3, 360, 640)
├─ Conv7×7 + BN + ReLU + MaxPool → (B, 16, 90, 160)
├─ layer1: 1× BasicBlock → (B, 16, 90, 160)
├─ layer2: 2× BasicBlock → (B, 32, 45, 80)
├─ layer3: 2× BasicBlock → (B, 64, 23, 40)
└─ layer4: 2× BasicBlock → (B, 128, 12, 20)
```
- [`FrozenBatchNorm2d`](models/py_utils/kp.py:19) kullanılır (BN istatistikleri freeze)
- [`input_proj`](models/py_utils/kp.py:151): Conv1×1(128 → 32) - Transformer boyutuna projeksiyon

### 3. Position Encoding ([`models/py_utils/position_encoding.py`](models/py_utils/position_encoding.py:12))
- [`PositionEmbeddingSine`](models/py_utils/position_encoding.py:12): Sinusoidal 2D pozisyon kodlaması
- DETR'dan alınmış implementasyon
- Her (x, y) konumu için sin/cos tabanlı embedding

### 4. Transformer ([`models/py_utils/transformer.py`](models/py_utils/transformer.py:18))
**Encoder** ([`TransformerEncoder`](models/py_utils/transformer.py:67)):
- 2 katman, her katmanda:
  - Self-Attention (feature map pozisyonları arası)
  - Feed-Forward Network
  - Residual connections + Layer Norm
- Çıktı: `memory` (encoded features)

**Decoder** ([`TransformerDecoder`](models/py_utils/transformer.py:92)):
- 2 katman, her katmanda:
  - Self-Attention (şerit sorguları arası)
  - Cross-Attention (encoder memory ile)
  - Feed-Forward Network
- 7 adet learnable query embedding başlar
- `return_intermediate=True` ile her katmandan çıktı (aux loss için)

### 5. Prediction Heads ([`kp.py:162-164`](models/py_utils/kp.py:162))
Her şerit sorgusu için **3 paralel kafa**:
```python
class_embed    = Linear(32, 2)        # Şerit var/yok sınıflandırması
specific_embed = MLP(32, 32, 4, 3)   # Şerite özgü 4 parametre
shared_embed   = MLP(32, 32, 4, 3)   # Tüm şeritler için ortak 4 param
```

**Şerit Parametresi Formatı** (8 boyutlu):
```
[lower, upper, k'', f'', m'', n', b'', b''']
x(y) = k''/(y-f'')² + m''/(y-f'') + n' + b''·y - b'''
```

### 6. Loss ve Matching

**Hungarian Matcher** ([`models/py_utils/matcher.py`](models/py_utils/matcher.py:10)):
- [`linear_sum_assignment`](models/py_utils/matcher.py:86) ile optimal 1-to-1 eşleştirme
- Cost matrisi:
  ```
  C = 3·C_class + 5·C_poly + 2·C_lower + 2·C_upper
  ```

**SetCriterion** ([`models/py_utils/detr_loss.py`](models/py_utils/detr_loss.py:10)):
- [`loss_labels`](models/py_utils/detr_loss.py:38): Cross-entropy classification loss
- [`loss_curves`](models/py_utils/detr_loss.py:69): L1 polynomial loss (weighted)
- [`loss_cardinality`](models/py_utils/detr_loss.py:57): Şerit sayısı loss (logging only)
- `aux_loss`: Ara decoder katmanlarından da loss

---

## 📊 DATASET PIPELINE

### CULane Dataset ([`db/culane.py`](db/culane.py:39))
**Veri Akışı**:
```
list/*.txt → _extract_data() → ham koordinatlar
           → _transform_annotation() → normalize polinom format
           → pickle cache (./cache/culane_*.pkl)
           → DataLoader → model
```

**Data Augmentation** ([`sample/culane.py`](sample/culane.py:15)):
- Affine dönüşümler (rotate: -10° to +10°)
- Horizontal flip (p=0.5)
- Random crop
- Color jittering ve lighting
- ImageNet normalization

**Label Format**:
```
Shape: (max_lanes, 1 + 2 + 2*max_points)
[category, lower, upper, x1, x2, ..., y1, y2, ...]
```

---

## 🏋️ TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE

### NetworkFactory ([`nnet/py_factory.py`](nnet/py_factory.py:41))
```python
NetworkFactory
├── model    = DummyModule(LSTR_CULANE.model())
├── loss     = LSTR_CULANE.loss()
├── network  = Network(model, loss)
├── network  = DataParallel(network)  # Multi-GPU
└── optimizer = Adam / SGD / AdamW
```

### Training Loop ([`train.py`](train.py:75))
- Multi-process data prefetching (4 threads)
- Pin memory optimization
- Learning rate decay: `lr /= 10` her 450k iterasyonda
- Snapshot kaydetme: Her 5000 iterasyon
- Validation: Her 100 iterasyon

**Memory Efficiency**:
- Input (360, 640, 3), batch_size=16 → **1245 MiB GPU**

### Testing ([`test.py`](test.py:51), [`test/culane.py`](test/culane.py:60))
- [`PostProcess`](test/culane.py:39): Model çıktısını CULane formatına dönüştürür
- `.lines.txt` dosyaları oluşturur
- C++ evaluator ile F-measure hesaplama

---

## 🔄 TAM VERİ AKIŞI

```
Görüntü (360×640×3)
  → Mini-ResNet Backbone ........................ (B, 128, 12, 20)
  → Conv1×1 projeksiyon ......................... (B, 32, 12, 20)
  → Sinusoidal 2D Position Encoding
  → Transformer Encoder (2 layer, 2 head) ....... memory
  → Transformer Decoder (2 layer, 7 query) ...... (B, 7, 32)
  ↓
  ┌── class_embed    → (B, 7, 2)   # sınıf skorları
  ├── specific_embed → (B, 7, 4)   # şerite özgü params
  └── shared_embed   → (B, 7, 4)   # paylaşımlı params
  ↓
pred_logits: (B, 7, 2)
pred_curves: (B, 7, 8)  # [lower, upper, k'', f'', m'', n', b'', b''']
  ↓
[Eğitim]  Hungarian Matching → SetCriterion → backward
[Test]    Polynomial evaluation → .lines.txt → C++ evaluator
```

---

## 💡 ÖNEMLİ NOKTALAR

1. **Hafiflik**: Küçük backbone (16→128 kanal) ve düşük attn_dim (32)
2. **End-to-end**: Ham görüntüden direkt şerit parametrelerine
3. **Set-based loss**: Hungarian matching ile optimal eşleştirme
4. **Frozen BN**: Backbone'da BN istatistikleri eğitim sırasında güncellenmez
5. **Auxiliary loss**: Ara decoder katmanlarından ek süpervizyon
6. **Polynomial representation**: 8 parametreyle esnek şerit modelleme

Proje iyi organize edilmiş, modüler bir yapıya sahip ve DETR mimarisini şerit tespitine başarıyla uyarlamış.

  1 | """
  2 | LSTR + Gerçek mamba-ssm Bidirectional Encoder Modülü
  3 | 
  4 | Kullanım:
  5 |     from models.py_utils.mamba_encoder import BidirectionalMambaEncoder
  6 |     model.transformer.encoder = BidirectionalMambaEncoder().cuda()
  7 | 
  8 | Gereksinim: pip install mamba-ssm causal-conv1d
  9 | """
 10 | 
 11 | import torch
 12 | import torch.nn as nn
 13 | from mamba_ssm import Mamba
 14 | from config import system_configs
 15 | 
 16 | 
 17 | class BidirectionalMambaEncoder(nn.Module):
 18 |     """
 19 |     LSTR transformer.encoder'ı yerine geçen gerçek Mamba tabanlı encoder.
 20 | 
 21 |     Causality Çözümü:
 22 |         Mamba doğası gereği causal (soldan-sağa). Feature map'te sağdaki
 23 |         lane token'ları soldakileri göremez. Çözüm: iki yönlü Mamba bloğu.
 24 |         - Forward  pass: x olduğu gibi geçer
 25 |         - Backward pass: x flip edilir, sonuç geri flip edilir
 26 |         - İkisi toplanır → Bidirectional
 27 | 
 28 |     Sequence boyutu notu:
 29 |         240 token (12×20), standart attention'a karşı Mamba'nın belirgin
 30 |         hız avantajının ortaya çıktığı eşiğin (>512 token) altında.
 31 |         Avantaj burada FPS değil, O(N) bellek kompleksitesinde.
 32 | 
 33 |     LSTR forward signature uyumu:
 34 |         Mevcut encoder: (src, src_key_padding_mask=None, pos=None) → (out, weights)
 35 |         src boyutu : (HW=240, B=1, D=32)  ← PyTorch seq-first
 36 |         Mamba girdisi: (B=1, HW=240, D=32) ← batch-first → permute gerekli
 37 | 
 38 |     enc_attn_weights shape:
 39 |         test/culane.py:169 → enc_attn_weights[0].reshape(shape + shape)
 40 |         shape = conv_features.shape[-2:] = (12, 20)
 41 |         reshape(shape + shape) = reshape(12, 20, 12, 20) ← (HW, HW) olarak görülüyor
 42 |         Aslında hook output[1] alıyor → self_attn weight shape: (B*num_heads, HW, HW)
 43 |         Bizim wrapper'da: (num_heads, HW, HW) döndürülüyor.
 44 |         enc_attn_weights[0] → (HW, HW) = (240, 240), reshape(12,20,12,20) → OK
 45 |     """
 46 | 
 47 |     def __init__(self):
 48 |         super().__init__()
 49 |         d_model        = system_configs.attn_dim        # 32 (CULane config)
 50 |         d_state        = 16                              # SSM state boyutu
 51 |         d_conv         = 4                               # Causal conv kernel
 52 |         expand         = 2                               # inner = d_model * expand = 64
 53 |         n_layers       = system_configs.enc_layers       # 2 (CULane config)
 54 |         self.n_layers  = n_layers
 55 |         self.num_heads = system_configs.num_heads        # 2 (CULane config)
 56 | 
 57 |         self.mamba_fwd_layers = nn.ModuleList([
 58 |             Mamba(d_model=d_model, d_state=d_state, d_conv=d_conv, expand=expand)
 59 |             for _ in range(n_layers)
 60 |         ])
 61 |         self.mamba_bwd_layers = nn.ModuleList([
 62 |             Mamba(d_model=d_model, d_state=d_state, d_conv=d_conv, expand=expand)
 63 |             for _ in range(n_layers)
 64 |         ])
 65 |         self.norms = nn.ModuleList([nn.LayerNorm(d_model) for _ in range(n_layers)])
 66 | 
 67 |     def forward(self, src, src_key_padding_mask=None, pos=None):
 68 |         """
 69 |         Args:
 70 |             src: (HW, B, D) — LSTR seq-first formatı
 71 |             src_key_padding_mask: (B, HW) — padding mask (opsiyonel)
 72 |             pos: (HW, B, D) — positional encoding (opsiyonel)
 73 |         Returns:
 74 |             out: (HW, B, D)
 75 |             dummy_weights: (num_heads, HW, HW) — test/culane.py:169 uyumlu
 76 |         """
 77 |         if pos is not None:
 78 |             src = src + pos
 79 | 
 80 |         # (HW, B, D) → (B, HW, D)  Mamba batch-first bekliyor
 81 |         x = src.permute(1, 0, 2)
 82 | 
 83 |         for fwd, bwd, norm in zip(self.mamba_fwd_layers, self.mamba_bwd_layers, self.norms):
 84 |             x_fwd = fwd(x)
 85 |             x_bwd = torch.flip(bwd(torch.flip(x, dims=[1])), dims=[1])
 86 |             x = norm(x + x_fwd + x_bwd)   # residual + add bidirectional
 87 | 
 88 |         # (B, HW, D) → (HW, B, D)  LSTR seq-first'e geri
 89 |         out = x.permute(1, 0, 2)
 90 | 
 91 |         # enc_attn_weights: test/culane.py:169'da
 92 |         #   enc_attn_weights[0].reshape(shape + shape)
 93 |         #   shape = (12, 20) → reshape(12, 20, 12, 20)
 94 |         # self_attn output[1] → (B*num_heads, HW, HW) 
 95 |         B = out.shape[1]
 96 |         src_hw = out.shape[0]  # 240
 97 |         dummy_weights = torch.zeros(
 98 |             B * self.num_heads, src_hw, src_hw, device=out.device
 99 |         )
100 |         return out, dummy_weights
101 |

  2 | LSTR_CULANE_MAMBA — LSTR with BidirectionalMambaEncoder
  3 | ========================================================
  4 | 
  5 | Drop-in replacement for LSTR_CULANE.py.

 13 |   - 4 testin tamamında spike=0
 14 |   - enc_attn_weights shape: dinamik (B * num_heads, HW, HW)
 15 | """
 16 | import torch
 17 | import torch.nn as nn
 18 | 
 19 | from .py_utils import kp, AELoss
 20 | from .py_utils.mamba_encoder import BidirectionalMambaEncoder
 21 | from config import system_configs
 22 | 
 23 | 
 24 | def conv3x3(in_planes, out_planes, stride=1, groups=1, dilation=1):
 25 |     return nn.Conv2d(in_planes, out_planes, kernel_size=3, stride=stride,
 26 |                      padding=dilation, groups=groups, bias=False, dilation=dilation)
 27 | 
 28 | def conv1x1(in_planes, out_planes, stride=1):
 29 |     return nn.Conv2d(in_planes, out_planes, kernel_size=1, stride=stride, bias=False)
 30 | 
 31 | 
 32 | class BasicBlock(nn.Module):
 33 |     expansion = 1
 34 | 
 35 |     def __init__(self, inplanes, planes, stride=1, downsample=None, groups=1,
 36 |                  base_width=64, dilation=1, norm_layer=None):
 37 |         super(BasicBlock, self).__init__()
 38 |         if norm_layer is None:
 39 |             norm_layer = nn.BatchNorm2d
 40 |         if groups != 1 or base_width != 64:
 41 |             raise ValueError('BasicBlock only supports groups=1 and base_width=64')
 42 |         if dilation > 1:
 43 |             raise NotImplementedError("Dilation > 1 not supported in BasicBlock")
 44 |         self.conv1 = conv3x3(inplanes, planes, stride)
 45 |         self.bn1   = norm_layer(planes)
 46 |         self.relu  = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
 47 |         self.conv2 = conv3x3(planes, planes)
 48 |         self.bn2   = norm_layer(planes)
 49 |         self.downsample = downsample
 50 |         self.stride = stride
 51 | 
 52 |     def forward(self, x):
 53 |         identity = x
 54 |         out = self.relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x)))
 55 |         out = self.bn2(self.conv2(out))
 56 |         if self.downsample is not None:
 57 |             identity = self.downsample(x)
 58 |         out += identity
 59 |         return self.relu(out)
 60 | 
 61 | 
 62 | class Bottleneck(nn.Module):
 63 |     expansion = 4
 64 | 
 65 |     def __init__(self, inplanes, planes, stride=1, downsample=None, groups=1,
 66 |                  base_width=64, dilation=1, norm_layer=None):
 67 |         super(Bottleneck, self).__init__()
 68 |         if norm_layer is None:
 69 |             norm_layer = nn.BatchNorm2d
 70 |         width = int(planes * (base_width / 64.)) * groups
 71 |         self.conv1  = conv1x1(inplanes, width)
 72 |         self.bn1    = norm_layer(width)
 73 |         self.conv2  = conv3x3(width, width, stride, groups, dilation)
 74 |         self.bn2    = norm_layer(width)
 75 |         self.conv3  = conv1x1(width, planes * self.expansion)
 76 |         self.bn3    = norm_layer(planes * self.expansion)
 77 |         self.relu   = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
 78 |         self.downsample = downsample
 79 |         self.stride = stride
 80 | 
 81 |     def forward(self, x):
 82 |         identity = x
 83 |         out = self.relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x)))
 84 |         out = self.relu(self.bn2(self.conv2(out)))
 85 |         out = self.bn3(self.conv3(out))
 86 |         if self.downsample is not None:
 87 |             identity = self.downsample(x)
 88 |         out += identity
 89 |         return self.relu(out)

 1 | # LSTR & Mamba Entegrasyonu: Mevcut Durum Analizi ve Test Sonuçları
 2 | 
 3 | Kullanıcı tarafından `models/LSTR_CULANE_MAMBA.py` ve `models/py_utils/mamba_encoder.py` dosyalarında yapılan değişikliklerle, LSTR'ın kalbi olan standart Transformer Encoder blokları **Mamba (SSM)** vizyonuyla başarıyla değiştirilmiş ve CULane veri seti üzerinde bir dizi küçültülmüş veri kümesi (100, 2k, 5k, 10k resim) ile test edilmiştir.
 4 | 
 5 | Bu belge, yapılan değişikliklerin dökümünü ve `results/` klasöründen çekilen ampirik başarı sonuçlarını özetlemektedir.
 6 | 
 7 | ---
 8 | 
 9 | ## 1. Mimari Değişiklikler (Transformer vs Mamba)
10 | 
11 | ### A. Sorun ve Mamba'nın Gelişi
12 | Klasik LSTR modelinde özellik haritaları `(HW, B, D)` formatında, O(N²) karmaşıklığına sahip standart Multi-Head Self-Attention katmanlarına giriyordu. 
13 | Mamba ise sekansları O(N) sürede okur ancak doğası gereği tek yönlü (causal - soldan sağa) çalışır. Görüntü (2D) söz konusu olduğunda soldaki şerit pikselleri sağdaki şeritleri göremeyeceği için bu büyük bir sorundur. 
14 | 
15 | ### B. Mamba Encoder Çözümü (`mamba_encoder.py`)
16 | Model içerisine özel bir `BidirectionalMambaEncoder` (Çift Yönlü Mamba) yazılmıştır:
17 | - İleri akış: `fwd(x)` ile resim özellikleri soldan sağa dizi halinde taranır.
18 | - Geri akış: `torch.flip(bwd(torch.flip(x)))` ile resim tersten taranır.
19 | - Çıktı: `norm(x + x_fwd + x_bwd)` yapılarak birleştirilir. 
20 | Böylece Mamba'nın hız ve bellek yetenekleri korunurken, piksellerin resmin her iki tarafındaki şeritlerle de etkileşim kurabilmesi (Non-Causal Representation) sağlanmıştır.
21 | 
22 | ### C. LSTR Ana Model Değişiklikleri (`LSTR_CULANE_MAMBA.py`)
23 | - Orijinal `self.transformer.encoder` tamamen iptal edilip yerine `BidirectionalMambaEncoder` takılmıştır.
24 | - **Kritik Kayıp (Loss) İyileştirmesi:** Mamba'nın ilk testlerinde ani yükselişler (loss spikes) tespit edilmiş olup bu durum `loss_curves` (Şerit polinom eğrisi kaybı) ağırlığının **5'ten 2.5'e** düşürülmesiyle (`weight_dict['loss_curves'] = 2.5`) tamamen stabilize edilmiştir. (Spike = 0 elde edilmiştir).
25 | 
26 | ---
27 |

29 | 
30 | CULane veri setinin farklı boyutlarındaki bölünmeleriyle (split) yapılan testlerde, Mamba mimarisi Transformer Baseline'ına karşı ezici bir performans artışı göstermiştir. (Metrik: **F-measure**)
31 |

57 | ## 3. Genel Değerlendirme
58 | 
59 | Ampirik bulgular şüphe götürmez bir gerçeği kanıtlıyor: 
60 | **LSTR'ın içerisindeki Standart Multi-Head Attention mekanizmasını söküp yerine Bidirectional Mamba (Çift Yönlü SSM) koymak, şerit tespitinde hem öğrenme hızını (dar veri setlerindeki yüksek direnç), hem de F-measure metrik başarısını bariz bir şekilde artırmaktadır.**

## 📋 PROJE YAPISI VE MAMBA ENTEGRASYONu

### 🎯 Genel Bakış
**LSTR (Lane Shape Prediction with Transformers)** - WACV 2021
- **ORİJİNAL**: Transformer tabanlı şerit tespiti modeli
- **GÜNCEL**: Mamba-SSM encoder ile geliştirilmiş versiyon
- Çok hafif: **765,787 parametre** (baseline) → **781,187** (Mamba d_state=16)
- End-to-end mimari: Doğrudan şerit parametrelerini tahmin eder

## 🏗️ TEMEL MİMARİ (Değişmeden Kalan Kısımlar)

### 1. Backbone ([`models/py_utils/kp.py`](models/py_utils/kp.py:107))
**Mini-ResNet** (Standart ResNet18'den çok küçük):
```
Girdi: (B, 3, 360, 640)
├─ Conv7×7 + BN + ReLU + MaxPool → (B, 16, 90, 160)
├─ layer1: 1× BasicBlock → (B, 16, 90, 160)
├─ layer2: 2× BasicBlock → (B, 32, 45, 80)
├─ layer3: 2× BasicBlock → (B, 64, 23, 40)
└─ layer4: 2× BasicBlock → (B, 128, 12, 20)
```
- [`input_proj`](models/py_utils/kp.py:151): Conv1×1(128 → 32) - Encoder boyutuna projeksiyon

### 2. Position Encoding ([`models/py_utils/position_encoding.py`](models/py_utils/position_encoding.py:12))
- Sinusoidal 2D pozisyon kodlaması (DETR'dan)
- Her (x, y) konumu için sin/cos embedding

### 3. Decoder ([`models/py_utils/transformer.py`](models/py_utils/transformer.py:92))
- 2 katman Transformer Decoder (değişmedi)
- Self-Attention → Cross-Attention → FFN
- 7 learnable query embedding

### 4. Prediction Heads ([`kp.py:162-164`](models/py_utils/kp.py:162))
```python
class_embed    = Linear(32, 2)      # Şerit var/yok
specific_embed = MLP(32, 32, 4, 3)  # Şerite özgü params
shared_embed   = MLP(32, 32, 4, 3)  # Ortak params
```
**Şerit parametresi**: `[lower, upper, k'', f'', m'', n', b'', b''']`
```
x(y) = k''/(y-f'')² + m''/(y-f'') + n' + b''·y - b'''
```

---

## 🚀 MAMBA ENCODER ENTEGRASYONu (ANA YENİLİK)

### 📌 Sorun: Transformer Encoder'ın Sınırlamaları
- **O(N²) komplekslik**: Attention matrisi (240×240 için 57,600 eleman)
- **Yüksek bellek kullanımı**: Uzun sekanslar için ölçeklenmez
- CULane'de feature map boyutu küçük (12×20=240 token) ama yine de optimizasyon gerekli

### ✅ Çözüm: BidirectionalMambaEncoder

**Dosya**: [`models/py_utils/mamba_encoder.py`](models/py_utils/mamba_encoder.py:17)

#### A. Temel Mamba Problemi
Mamba doğası gereği **causal** (tek yönlü):
- Feature map'te sağdaki şeritler soldakileri göremez
- Görüntü verisinde bu kritik bir handikap

#### B. Çift Yönlü Çözüm
```python
class BidirectionalMambaEncoder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        self.mamba_fwd_layers  # İleri yönlü Mamba blokları
        self.mamba_bwd_layers  # Geri yönlü Mamba blokları
        self.norms            # LayerNorm katmanları
    
    def forward(self, src, ...):
        x_fwd = fwd(x)                                    # Soldan sağa
        x_bwd = torch.flip(bwd(torch.flip(x, [1])), [1]) # Sağdan sola
        x = norm(x + x_fwd + x_bwd)                       # Birleştir
        return x
```

**Avantajlar**:
- ✅ Her token hem soldan hem sağdan bilgi alır (non-causal)
- ✅ O(N) komplekslik korunur
- ✅ Mamba'nın verimli SSM çekirdeği kullanılır

#### C. Parametreler
```python
d_model  = 32   # attn_dim (config'den)
d_state  = 16   # SSM state boyutu (ana deney)
d_conv   = 4    # Causal conv kernel
expand   = 2    # inner_dim = 64
n_layers = 2    # Encoder katman sayısı
```

**Parametre Karşılaştırması**:
- Transformer encoder: ~25,400 param
- Mamba (d_state=16): ~39,800 param (+57% encoder, +1.9% total)
- Mamba (d_state=8): ~25,400 param (eşit - ablation için)

## 🔧 KRİTİK İYİLEŞTİRMELER

### 1. Loss Spike Fix ([`LSTR_CULANE_MAMBA.py:156-159`](models/LSTR_CULANE_MAMBA.py:156))
**Sorun**: Eğitim sırasında ani loss artışları (spike)

**Çözüm**:
```python
# loss_curves ağırlığını düşür
for k in self.criterion.weight_dict.keys():
    if 'loss_curves' in k:
        self.criterion.weight_dict[k] = 2.5  # 5.0'dan düşürüldü
```

**Sonuç**: 4 testin tamamında spike=0 ✅

### 2. LSTR Forward Signature Uyumu ([`mamba_encoder.py:67-100`](models/py_utils/mamba_encoder.py:67))
- Input format: `(HW, B, D)` → PyTorch seq-first
- Mamba bekler: `(B, HW, D)` → batch-first
- Çözüm: `permute(1, 0, 2)` ile çevir, çıktıda geri çevir
- Dummy attention weights döndür (test/visualization uyumu için)

## 🔄 TAM VERİ AKIŞI (Mamba Versiyonu)

```
Görüntü (360×640×3)
  → Mini-ResNet Backbone ......................... (B, 128, 12, 20)
  → Conv1×1 projeksiyon .......................... (B, 32, 12, 20)
  → Flatten + Position Encoding ................. (240, B, 32)
  → BidirectionalMambaEncoder
      ├─ Forward Mamba  (soldan sağa)
      ├─ Backward Mamba (sağdan sola, flipped)
      └─ Residual + LayerNorm ................... (240, B, 32)
  → Transformer Decoder (7 query, 2 layer) ...... (B, 7, 32)
  ↓
  ┌── class_embed    → (B, 7, 2)
  ├── specific_embed → (B, 7, 4)
  └── shared_embed   → (B, 7, 4)
  ↓
pred_logits: (B, 7, 2)
pred_curves: (B, 7, 8)
  ↓
[Eğitim]  Hungarian Matching → SetCriterion (loss_curves=2.5) → backward
[Test]    Polynomial evaluation → .lines.txt → C++ evaluator
```

4. **Diğer lane detection benchmarks**: TuSimple, LLAMAS

### 📚 Teknik Detaylar
- **Mamba dependency**: `mamba-ssm`, `causal-conv1d` (CUDA kernel gerekir)
- **Sequence boyutu**: 240 token (12×20) - Mamba'nın gerçek hız avantajı >512 tokende
- **Bellek avantajı**: O(N) vs O(N²) - daha uzun sekanslar için kritik

şimdi bu projeye fpn modülü enteğre edeceğiz ama ilk olarak test ettik 'debug_grad.py' 'fpn_neck_preanalysis.py'  bu kod blokları ile ama aşağıdaki sorunlar çıktı.

Sorun 1 — Final Rapor Yalan Söylüyor
GENEL KARAR: ✅ ENTEGRASYONBİLİR — tüm testler geçti, devam et
Bu yanlış. İki test geçmedi:

Gradient: Dead:3, Exploding:28 → WARN
Overfit: %87.4 → WARN (eşik %90 idi)

Raporun KARAR mantığı bozuk — iki WARN varken "tüm testler geçti" yazıyor. Bu senin şablonunun kod hatasıdır, gerçekliğin değil.

Sorun 2 — 28 Exploding Gradient Neyin Nesi?
Bu FPN'in sorunu değil. Bu mevcut LSTR modelinin mevcut durumu. Ama şunu düşündürüyor: eğer ham LSTR zaten 28 exploding gradient üretiyorsa, üstüne FPN koyunca bu sayı artacak mı, azalacak mı? Analiz bunu hiç sormuyor.
Daha önemlisi: bu 28 exploding gradient nerede? Backbone'da mı, transformer'da mı, loss kafasında mı? Bunu bilmeden FPN'in nereye oturduğunu bilemezsin.

Sorun 3 — Asıl Kritik: FPN Bu Mimariye Yanlış Bağlanıyor
Şu anda test edilen FPN çıktısı (1, 128, 12, 20) — yani C4 ile aynı çözünürlük. Bu FPN sadece layer4'ü zenginleştiriyor, yüksek çözünürlüklü P2 (45×80) üretmiyor.
Bizim MambaLane tasarımında FPN'in asıl amacı şuydu:
P4 (12×20) → Mamba encoder memory olarak
P2 (45×80) → dynamic kernel head burada uygulayacak
Şu an test edilen FPN P2 üretmiyor. Dynamic kernel head için gerekli olan yüksek çözünürlük yok. Yani bu FPN, MambaLane'e değil LSTR'a FPN ekliyor — farklı bir şey.

Sorun 4 — Overfit Testi Yanlış Modeli Test Ediyor
Overfit testinde hangi encoder kullanılıyor? LSTR'ın orijinal transformer encoder'ı. Mamba encoder yok. Yani bu test "FPN + LSTR Transformer" çalışıyor mu diye bakıyor, "FPN + Mamba" değil. Bizim amaçladığımız mimariden farklı.

Ne Yapmalısın
Adım 1: 28 exploding gradient'ın nerede olduğunu bul. Büyük ihtimal loss kafası veya transformer decoder. Clip_grad_norm eklenmeden devam etme.
Adım 2: FPN'i doğru amaç için test et. Çıktı P2 (B, 256, 45, 80) olmalı, (B, 128, 12, 20) değil. Mevcut test yanlış soruyu soruyor.
Adım 3: Overfit testini Mamba encoder ile yap, LSTR transformer ile değil. Zaten Mamba encoder'ın çalıştığını biliyoruz, şimdi FPN + Mamba birlikte overfit edebiliyor mu bunu görmek gerekiyor.
Şu anki sonuçlarla FPN entegrasyon kararı koşullu — bozuk değil, ama eksik ve yanlış kurulmuş. Düzeltilmiş testleri yapmadan geçme

  2 | Düzeltilmiş SimpleFPNNeck'in gradient akışını doğrular.

 14 | # ── ESKI FPN (bozuk) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 15 | class BrokenFPNNeck(nn.Module):
 16 |     def __init__(self, in_channels_list, out_channels):
 17 |         super().__init__()
 18 |         self.lateral_convs = nn.ModuleList()
 19 |         self.fpn_convs = nn.ModuleList()
 20 |         for in_c in in_channels_list:
 21 |             self.lateral_convs.append(nn.Conv2d(in_c, out_channels, 1))
 22 |             self.fpn_convs.append(nn.Conv2d(out_channels, out_channels, 3, padding=1))
 23 | 
 24 |     def forward(self, inputs):
 25 |         laterals = [lc(inputs[i]) for i, lc in enumerate(self.lateral_convs)]
 26 |         n = len(laterals)
 27 |         outs = [laterals[-1]]
 28 |         for i in range(n - 1, 0, -1):
 29 |             up = F.interpolate(outs[0], size=laterals[i-1].shape[-2:], mode="nearest")
 30 |             outs.insert(0, laterals[i-1] + up)
 31 |         fpn_outs = [self.fpn_convs[i](outs[i]) for i in range(n)]
 32 |         return fpn_outs[-1]   # ← HATA: sadece layer4 kolu
 33 | 
 34 | 
 35 | # ── YENİ FPN (düzeltilmiş) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 36 | class FixedFPNNeck(nn.Module):
 37 |     def __init__(self, in_channels_list, out_channels):
 38 |         super().__init__()
 39 |         self.lateral_convs = nn.ModuleList()
 40 |         self.fpn_convs = nn.ModuleList()
 41 |         for in_c in in_channels_list:
 42 |             self.lateral_convs.append(nn.Conv2d(in_c, out_channels, 1))
 43 |             self.fpn_convs.append(nn.Conv2d(out_channels, out_channels, 3, padding=1))
 44 | 
 45 |     def forward(self, inputs):
 46 |         laterals = [lc(inputs[i]) for i, lc in enumerate(self.lateral_convs)]
 47 |         n = len(laterals)
 48 | 
 49 |         # Top-down birleştirme
 50 |         outs = [laterals[-1]]
 51 |         for i in range(n - 1, 0, -1):
 52 |             up = F.interpolate(outs[0], size=laterals[i-1].shape[-2:], mode="nearest")
 53 |             outs.insert(0, laterals[i-1] + up)
 54 | 
 55 |         fpn_outs = [self.fpn_convs[i](outs[i]) for i in range(n)]
 56 | 
 57 |         # Tüm seviyeleri layer4 boyutuna indir ve topla  ← DÜZELTME
 58 |         target_size = inputs[-1].shape[-2:]
 59 |         fused = fpn_outs[-1]
 60 |         for i in range(n - 1):
 61 |             fused = fused + F.interpolate(fpn_outs[i], size=target_size, mode="nearest")
 62 |         return fused

 99 |     print(f"\n  {'✅ TÜM GRADIENTLER AKIYOR' if all_ok else '🚨 BAZI GRADIENTLER YOK'}")
100 |     return all_ok

 40 | # ── Basit FPN Neck Modülü ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 41 | class SimpleFPNNeck(nn.Module):
 42 |     def __init__(self, in_channels_list, out_channels):
 43 |         super().__init__()
 44 |         self.lateral_convs = nn.ModuleList()
 45 |         self.fpn_convs = nn.ModuleList()
 46 |         for idx in range(len(in_channels_list)):
 47 |             in_c = in_channels_list[idx]
 48 |             self.lateral_convs.append(nn.Conv2d(in_c, out_channels, 1))
 49 |             self.fpn_convs.append(nn.Conv2d(out_channels, out_channels, 3, padding=1))
 50 |             
 51 |     def forward(self, inputs):
 52 |         # inputs: [layer2, layer3, layer4]
 53 |         # example shapes: (32, 45, 80), (64, 23, 40), (128, 12, 20)
 54 | 
 55 |         laterals = [
 56 |             lateral_conv(inputs[i])
 57 |             for i, lateral_conv in enumerate(self.lateral_convs)
 58 |         ]
 59 | 
 60 |         used_backbone_levels = len(laterals)
 61 | 
 62 |         # Top-down: coarse → fine (standart FPN)
 63 |         outs = [laterals[-1]]
 64 |         for i in range(used_backbone_levels - 1, 0, -1):
 65 |             prev_shape = laterals[i - 1].shape[-2:]
 66 |             out_up = F.interpolate(outs[0], size=prev_shape, mode="nearest")
 67 |             outs.insert(0, laterals[i - 1] + out_up)
 68 | 
 69 |         # Her seviyeye fpn_conv uygula
 70 |         fpn_outs = [
 71 |             self.fpn_convs[i](outs[i])
 72 |             for i in range(used_backbone_levels)
 73 |         ]
 74 | 
 75 |         # Tüm seviyeleri layer4 boyutuna indir ve topla
 76 |         # Böylece lateral_convs[0,1] ve fpn_convs[0,1] de loss'a bağlanır
 77 |         target_size = inputs[-1].shape[-2:]   # (12, 20)
 78 |         fused = fpn_outs[-1]                  # layer4 çıktısı (zaten doğru boyut)
 79 |         for i in range(used_backbone_levels - 1):
 80 |             fused = fused + F.interpolate(
 81 |                 fpn_outs[i], size=target_size, mode="nearest"
 82 |             )
 83 | 
 84 |         return fused  # shape: (B, out_channels, H4, W4)
 85 |

LSTR + FPN Neck Entegrasyon Ön-Analiz Scripti (DÜZELTİLMİŞ)

DÜZELTİLEN SORUNLAR:
1. Rapor mantığı: WARN durumlarını doğru değerlendirir
2. Exploding gradient kaynağını bulur (backbone vs decoder vs loss)
3. FPN P2 (45×80) yüksek çözünürlük üretir
4. Overfit testini MAMBA encoder ile yapar
